#176030. England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 32m • 📚 Deep Dive (6411 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

England throw it away with defending unworthy of a top nation

📅 26 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 32 min read (6411 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~32 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • There had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA.
  • In a recent development, the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win.
  • Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN!
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

There had been so much talk – first raised by Thomas Tuchel after the shocking World Cup exit to Argentina – about England’s DNA. About whether they could keep the ball, pass the ball, control the ball, the way Spain do.

In a recent development, the world and European champions were England’s first opponents – after the World Cup – in this Nations League campaign and came away from Wembley with a deserved win. They are now 39 games unbeaten with substitute Mikel Oyarzabal, who scored the winning goal against England in the final of the last European Championship, doing so again.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

Sources indicate that that may have been no surprise, even if the inevitable “olés” after Spain’s third goal will have hurt. But the nature of it? For the England manager this was another shocker. Not in the way his team went about the task. They were positive, fun, attacking. But in the way they conceded – goals and chances – and lost.

On this performance, DNA, for England, stands for Defensively Not Able, as they threw away what could have been a famous and restorative victory. Instead, with Croatia beating the Czech Republic in the other group game, England are under immediate pressure to win in Prague on Tuesday.

In fact, England have conceded 13 goals in their past six matches – in fairness including four in that third-place World Cup 6-4 win over France – and that is not good enough for a top-tier nation. Tuchel needs to sort it out defensively.

It could have been very different if Harry Kane had not missed from the penalty spot, slipping as he struck the ball, with England improbably 2-1 ahead. “It would have been the decisive punch,” Tuchel stated. Maybe so, even if there was always the feeling that Spain could go through the gears.

Recent findings suggest that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

Afterwards there were claims, led by the impressive Anthony Gordon, that this was a missed opportunity for England. A bit like the World Cup. They need to shake this theme.

It has been revealed that the irony was this was one of their best creative displays for quite some time. They took the game to Spain and could have scored more. And conceded more.

In truth it could have been Spain 4 England 0 inside half an hour and before Tuchel’s team laid a glove on their opponents.

Another let off for England 😧Ferran Torres misses another significant chance one-on-one with James Trafford #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/KFkJoJUW6c.

The manager had also spoken about how England should “embrace the chaos” as their best route to success. That may appear a questionable tactic – does chaos ever win a tournament? – but England certainly did that. This was as chaotic and, admittedly, entertaining as it gets.

England attacked with pace and power with the pick of their players the two based in Spain: Gordon, who scored, and Jude Bellingham. And the defenders? This was a bad night for Marc Guéhi, his Manchester City team-mate Nico O’Reilly (cue speculation about whether they were distracted by the verdict on the Premier League charges against their club) and for Jarell Quansah at right-back who is so evidently a centre-half.

It has been revealed that A penny, once more, for the thoughts of the unused Trent Alexander-Arnold. The fourth defender, Ezri Konsa, vented his frustration at what was happening around him.

It was not just the errors but the unforced nature of them. Poor in possession with misplaced passes and defensively wide open. There is a gap between Spain and England but not as big as the gaps that were exposed in England’s back four. They endured a full house of calamities. They seemed strangely unaware – or incapable of dealing with – the danger posed by the outstanding Lamine Yamal.

Maybe because of the opposition – or the criticism – England felt the need to play out. But what an horrific start. What an inexplicable moment for Guéhi as he received the ball from O’Reilly and turned into trouble, gifting possession to Yamal who ran on and scored. Inside two minutes.

WHAT A START FROM SPAIN 🇪🇸Lamine Yamal pounces on a Marc Guéhi error to give Spain an early lead at Wembley #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/Et83EyTPlp.

Spain walked out with the second star on their shirt – to mark their second World Cup triumph. That was the star Tuchel had promised for England.

Now, straight away, they were up against it. It could have turned very ugly. Ferran Torres, who had scored the winner in the World Cup Final, had one disallowed for offside, then was thwarted by James Trafford after – inexplicably again – being played onside by Quansah.

BIG SAVE from James Trafford 🧤The Leeds United goalkeeper keeps out Ferran Torres#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/nj5b8AUSQU.

Sources indicate that then Torres was sent clear following Elliot Anderson’s poor pass, only to drag his shot wide. The third miss came from Dani Olmo, again set up by Yamal.

In a recent development, it could – it should – have been game over. Then England unexpectedly turned it around. They had kept attacking despite what was going on at the back and struck through a truly thrilling counter-attack, with Gordon and Bellingham combining before the Barcelona winger calmly beat goalkeeper Unai Simon.

It has been revealed that ENGLAND ARE LEVEL! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿A brilliant finish from Anthony Gordon after a breathtaking counter attack 👏#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/z0nSfWIHVd.

It was an exceptional goal and was promptly followed by a fortunate one as O’Reilly’s cross was met by Kane who stooped to steer in a header, only for it to strike Marc Cucurella, who made a mess of clearing, and it went past Simón.

I think we'll give that goal to Harry Kane 🎯England come from behind to lead Spain thanks Harry Kane, with assistance from Marc Cucurella ⚽️#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/X3qSOWUhVT.

The Spain left-back hit the post with a cross, misjudged by Trafford who was given this game and the next to stake his claim ahead of Jordan Pickford who has so long been the undisputed first-choice.

England dominated for a while and Bellingham won a penalty, after a VAR intervention, only for Kane to strike the crossbar.

How Spain made them pay and worryingly so. O’Reilly passed the ball straight to Olmo who swept it inside. Substitute Álex Baena checked and beat Trafford from the edge of the area. Even worse was how Spain cut through the heart of England defence with Baena finding Oyarzabal. Why was no defender closer to him? What was Guéhi doing? And O’Reilly? Oyarzabal exquisitely dinked the ball over Trafford.

Thomas Tuchel does not think Manchester City’s guilty verdict over almost all of their Premier League charges distracted his England players in the Nations League defeat to Spain.

City players Marc Guéhi and Nico O’Reilly were at fault for two of Spain’s goals and both Tuchel, the head coach, and England captain Harry Kane confirmed news of the verdict had been discussed among the squad.

Tuchel does not plan to address the matter with his players ahead of the remaining Nations League games against Czech Republic and Croatia.

Industry observers note that asked if the City verdict had been a cause of discussion ahead of the Spain game, Tuchel replied: “Not for me, but I can imagine maybe for the Man City players. I won’t comment on it as it’s an ongoing case.

“I didn’t make it a topic. It was not a topic for me. I’m just thinking about Spain and the team and meetings. The players have more time than me. So I can imagine they talk about it. It’s good they do. I don’t think it was a distraction for them.”.

Kane added: “There was a discussion, but when we’re with England, we kind of put club football to one side and it was no different this week.”.

Tuchel also refused to point the finger of blame at Guéhi, O’Reilly or Kane, who missed a penalty, for England’s defeat despite admitting his team got off to the worst possible start by conceding a goal after two minutes.

“We will focus on the positives, but also highlight the stuff we can do better,” Tuchel said. “Not even speaking about individual mistakes because this is normal. It just happens. It should not happen, and for sure not in this amount. But there is no sense in showing the individual mistakes or telling them ‘please don’t make mistakes’. That is normal, but we can do things better. We can defend the third goal better. But we will focus on the positives. There is a lot to take away from the game.

Sources indicate that “We wanted to be the team desperately to beat them [Spain] and we think we had them. We still think we had them at half-time. That was the way the team showed up after half-time. So we will focus on that, but the reality is we lost and the reality is we need to prove it again.”.

In a recent development, “It was a terrible start, the worst possible start, which makes it so difficult against a team like this. The reaction was very good. After 10/12 minutes, we were the better team but we gave away too many mistakes. We were the better team. If we had converted the penalty, it could have been the decisive moment. We have to keep going and learn from the mistakes. We could have created more if we had been more clinical in the final 20 metres. We showed great bravery and courage with our high-ball wins. There will always be moments you suffer against teams like this. The effort and quality were there tonight but the result does not prove it today.”.

“I think there is a gap [between Spain and England]. They [Spain] are the world champions and European champions. Mikel Oyarzabal was never going to miss. He was always in control of the situation. Honestly, people talk about sexy football, that is sexy football. I would watch that all night.”.

🗣️ "We went toe to toe with the European and world champions" 💪Harry Kane remains positive about England performance despite their 3-2 defeat to Spain 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿🇪🇸#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/qkhqsqmPEl.

🗣️ "You have to beat them to show people we can do this" 💪@IanWright0 reflects on England's 3-2 defeat to Spain at Wembley#ITVFootball | @markpougatch pic.twitter.com/ko2FYs4VqA.

According to recent reports, marc Guehi and Nico O’Reilly may want to look away now but Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon scored well. Our very own Mike McGrath has provided his player ratings.

Tonight: England 2 Spain 3 (H)Tuesday September 29: Czech Republic (A), kick-off 7.45pmSaturday October 3: Croatia (A), kick-off 5pmTuesday October 6: Czech Republic (H), kick-off 7.45pm.

🗣️ "I think it's a bit of a missed chance" 👀Anthony Gordon says mistakes cost England the win tonight against Spain at Wembley 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @gabrielclarke05 | @England pic.twitter.com/AJBxVNjbjq.

Sources indicate that A highly entertaining game. England will probably argue the game changed on Kane’s missed penalty, but Spain missed a lot of very clear chances and will feel they deserved the victory. A losing start to the Nations League for Tuchel and his team, but there were some positives. Gordon, Bellingham and Anderson were all excellent. Some of the defending, not so excellent.

Possession: England 47%-53% SpainShots: 13-15Shots on target: 5-5Corners: 6-3Touches in opposition box: 37-15.

Sources indicate that england have one last chance with a corner out on the left. This will be it. Spain are able to deal with it and clear their lines.

Sources indicate that then comes the final whistle at Wembley and the world champions Spain claim a 3-2 victory in north London. It was an absorbing game, where momentum swung one way and then the other, but it is Spain who are the victors.

Sources indicate that baena brings down Rogers with a silly challenge to gift England a free-kick deep in the Spanish half. This could be England’s last chance.

Anderson is over it but his delivery is poor, easily caught by Unai Simon.

England are running out of time to find an equaliser.

O’Reilly appears to be suffering with cramp but England have made all five substitutions.

There will be five added minutes.

A late change for England as Branthwaite replaces Guehi.

Rogers delivers a dangerous cross from the right that runs through the six-yard box and forces Pubill to put it behind for a corner.

England take it short before Anderson clips it in but Laporte heads away.

In a recent development, garner should have done so much better with that. His run into the Spain box on the left side is picked out by Anderson’s pass. Garner has Calvert-Lewin waiting at the back post but the former massively overhits the cross.

Double substitution from England as Calvert-Lewin and Gibbs-White replace Kane and Saka. Rare to say Kane taken off, especially when England are behind.

Saka goes down under a challenge from Cucurella inside the Spain penalty box but no penalty is forthcoming. VAR has cleared the incident. Moments later, Bellingham is then booked for stopping Spain going on the counter.

Spain make a change as Merino replaces Olmo.

Recent findings suggest that the way Spain control possession and keep the ball is impressive. They toy with you pretty well and often look so composed.

Baena, who has been superb since coming on, feeds a lovely pass into the path of Oyarzabal on the right side of the box. Oyarzabal takes one touch before lifting it over Trafford into the England net. That is a lovely assist from Baena and lovely finish from Oyarzabal.

Mikel Oyarzabal SCORES against England AGAIN! 🎯Spain retake the lead after a slick finish from the Spaniard 👏#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pPT3KvRHWl.

In a recent development, given the quality of the opposition and the sustained threat he carried, that might have been Gordon’s best-ever performance in an England shirt. Him and Bellingham have been excellent. But now he’s been replaced by Morgan Rogers.

Guehi joins O’Reilly in the book for a cynical foul on Olmo. You can put that yellow card in the category of a professional foul.

Industry observers note that england are making a double change as Garner and Rogers come on for Lewis-Skelly and Gordon. Garner was not in the initial squad but takes his chance now after the withdrawals.

Spain also make a substitution as Pedri replaces Ruiz.

At one end, Yamal has a shot blocked after England gave the ball away before Lewis-Skelly’s shot down the other end is easily saved.

The first booking of the night sees O’Reilly shown a yellow card for a foul on Yamal.

According to recent reports, england come close to going back in front. After good work from Bellingham, Saka has it on the right side of the box. Saka cuts inside onto his left and looks to pick out the far corner but his effort goes narrowly wide.

It has been revealed that another significant mistake from England is punished. It is absolutely dreadful from O’Reilly, who gives the ball away so poorly deep inside the England half. Spain capitalise and it is the man who has only just come on, Baena, who curls into the bottom corner from the edge of the box. All to play for with half an hour to go at Wembley.

SPAIN EQUALISE! 🇪🇸A brilliant finish from Alex Baena after a Nico O'Reilly mistake 🎯#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/tXygPfbPmb.

Yamal and Baena exchange a lovely one-two on the right side of the box and you think the former will find the far corner but his effort goes wide.

Industry observers note that how did Yamal MISS that! 🤯A massive opportunity goes begging to pull Spain level! #ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/jyzLm9VBd5.

Industry observers note that cucurella has a real habit of making himself unpopular wherever he plays. The Wembley crowd have been booing his every touch and were not happy with him staying down after the ball hit him in the head. Spain haven’t got going at all in this second half.

Spain have made a double change as Oyarzabal and Baena replace Torres and Williams.

Kane steps up but his effort smashes into the bar. Kane slipped just as he took it. In fact, a free-kick is given to Spain as it was a double hit.

Industry observers note that kane MISSES from the penalty spot! 😧Harry Kane slips when he strikes the ball, let off for Spain and Luis de la Fuente#ITVFootball pic.twitter.com/pvg3GGa9ma.

It has been revealed that the referee overturns the original decision and points to the spot. A foul from a Barcelona midfielder on a Real Madrid midfielder is given.

In a recent development, yet more England appeals for a penalty. Bellingham goes down, believing he was fouled by Rodri, but the referee gives nothing. There is contact but is it enough for a penalty? The referee had a good view and there is a decent shout for a penalty.

The referee is being sent to the screen so we know what that usually means...

Sources indicate that certainly no sitting on the lead from England at the start of the second half. Tuchel was adamant that Bellingham should have been awarded a penalty after going down in the area.

And Tuchel might get his way as VAR have sent referee Davide Massa to the screen.

Sources indicate that england want a penalty. Saka goes down under a challenge from Laporte from behind but those appeals are waved away. VAR checks and clears the incident. Laporte got the ball.

It has been revealed that chance for England. Bellingham’s cross from the left picks out Quansah in the centre of the box but the defender’s header from eight yards out misses the target. What an opportunity that was for Quansah to score his first international goal.

Sources indicate that spain are unbeaten in nearly 40 competitive matches and, as it stands, that run is set to come to an end. Still a long way to come though tonight and Spain could have been 3-0 up before England even scored one goal.

We are back under way at Wembley. No changes for either side at the break.

During half-time, Kyle Walker received a framed shirt to celebrate his 96 England caps.

According to recent reports, what a response from our #ThreeLions! 💪 pic.twitter.com/qBoY0J79JL.

2 - Lamine Yamal has scored the third quickest goal England have ever conceded at Wembley Stadium, behind only first minute goals for Scotland in 1957 and Hungary in 1953.Punch. pic.twitter.com/NxVp1qOnVi.

Possession: England 45%-55% SpainShots: 6-8Shots on target: 2-2Corners: 3-3Touches in opposition box: 10-10.

Tuchel will be delighted with the half-time score and England’s spirit after going behind so early. But how on earth have Spain only scored once? They’ve missed a couple of one-on-ones, hit the post and blazed over the bar. Highly entertaining and England will know they will have to defend better if they are going to hold on to their lead.

In a recent development, an absorbing and end-to-end first half is brought to an end. Somehow, despite the fact at one point they could have been 3-0 down, England lead 2-1 at the break.

According to recent reports, cucurella’s cross from the left loops all the way to the back post, where it strikes the frame of the goal. I do not think Cucurella meant that.

There will be one added minute.

Sources indicate that it is chances galore at both ends, with the latest falling to Ruiz, whose shot from the edge of the box is deflected wide for a corner. Bellingham heads away at the front post.

England gift the ball away so poorly and Yamal should punish them with his second goal of the game but he blazes high over the bar.

Industry observers note that what on earth has happened to Spain? O’Reilly’s cross from the byline picks out Kane, who guides a header towards goal. Cucurella makes an absolute mess of things, effectively kneeing the ball past his keeper and into his own net. Kane will try and claim it but surely that has to go down as an own goal. 10 minutes ago, Spain should have been 3-0 up. Now, England are 2-1 ahead.

Harry Kane wants England to address how they lost their identity and went “against our beliefs” at the World Cup.

In a brutally honest assessment of the tournament, the England captain admitted Thomas Tuchel’s team did not play to their full potential in several games – even before the painful semi-final exit against Argentina.

Kane, who played golf instead of watching the World Cup final, revealed the 2-1 Atlanta defeat hurt more than missing a penalty four years earlier in Qatar, when England were knocked out by France in the quarter-finals.

“This one hurt more than any other one. I would probably say even more than when I missed a penalty in Qatar because of the manner that it happened,” Kane remarked. “It was not us as a team.

“We trust our players and the player know very well that if you miss a camp then someone plays well in your position that the competition is always on. You have to make sure to be available and to produce top-level performances in camp and if you do so, that counts for something. Right now, it is not on my list of worries. I am not wired like this. From the moment I arrived at SGP my full focus is 100 per cent with the players who are here.

“There is no threat, distrust or threat of consequences. It will come naturally. I truly believe that we have the opposite. You will talk to our captain, Harry Kane, who has the most minutes for club and country and is happy to be here while teammates of his are enjoying a 10-day break. He is the role model and that is the vibe we have here.”.

They do have plenty to cheer about:.

James Trafford is poised to start for England ahead of Jordan Pickford against Spain tonight.

Pickford has been England’s No1 for eight years but Thomas Tuchel is set to make a change to face the world champions in the Nations League opener at Wembley.

Trafford went to the World Cup in the summer and has started the Premier League in good form following his move to Leeds.

In the first match since the World Cup, changing his goalkeeper is a major selection decision from Tuchel.

Elsewhere, Jarell Quansah is set to play at right-back ahead of Trent Alexander-Arnold while Myles Lewis-Skelly is also in line to return to the starting XI after being recalled into the squad after missing the World Cup.

England begin their Nations League campaign with a home game against the world champions Spain. This is England’s first game since the World Cup, with their dreams of glory ended by Argentina in the semi-finals, but they did finish third after beating France in a high-scoring third/fourth play-off. The last meeting between these sides saw Spain beat England to win Euro 2024. They also faced off in the Nations League back in 2018, with Spain winning at Wembley and England taking victory over in Spain.

England’s intends for these games has been disrupted by a number of withdrawals. Cole Palmer had earned a recall having been left out of the World Cup squad but the Chelsea forward has withdrawn due to a minor injury, despite playing the full game for Chelsea against Brentford in the final game before the international beak.

“He [Palmer] plays with discomfort and pain and cannot play on the highest level with discomfort and pain,” Tuchel mentioned. “Chelsea informed us. That is my understanding. We are not managing load. This is not an ‘international break’. It is a competitive environment, where the players love to train and be together. That is what we created. We will never compromise on that. We will never let this feeling creep in that the players do not want to come [to England camps]. We focus on the guys who absolutely want to play for England.

Sources indicate that “For sure it is a missed opportunity. It is another missed opportunity. He misses too many opportunities. I do not blame him for it, it is just a fact. He misses way too many camps with injuries. I only want to rely on what I personally witness and see within my team. For that you have to be in camp. If you are not in camp there is a next level to impress that you cannot achieve because you can only do it with me on the pitch and with us on the pitch. It is a missed opportunity.”.

Sources indicate that declan Rice has also withdrawn from the squad despite playing the full game in Arsenal’s defeat to Brighton as have Kobbie Mainoo, Marcus Rashford and Tino Livramento. Morgan Gibbs-White and James Garner have been called up as a result.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is back in the fold for the first time since June 2025. 18-year-old Liverpool winger Rio Ngumoha made his England debut against New Zealand during the World Cup warm-ups and takes his place in this squad, although he does make the matchday squad for tonight’s game. England will also take on Czechia, Croatia and then Cezchia again during this international break.

Industry observers note that having been crowned world champions back in July, Spain are now champions of both Europe and the world. Back in June 2025, Spain made the Nations League final but lost on penalties to Portugal. Ahead of this international window, The Royal Spanish Federation has extended Luis de la Fuente’s contract until 2032. After tonight, Spain will host Croatia and Czechia before travelling to Croatia to cap off this international window.

This is an extended international break, with four games to take place during this window. Team news from Wembley to follow shortly.

Published: 01:43 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 01:45 EST, 22 November 2026.

All eyes will be on Manchester United's newly introduced head coach Mauricio Pochettino when they take on Liverpool at Anfield this afternoon.

Sources indicate that liverpool manager Andoni Iraola has freshened up the squad since joining in the summer, including the £123million purchase of Bradley Barcola from Paris Saint-Germain, while blending in young emerging talent. They have made a solid start across all four competitions, knocking Chelsea out of the League Cup on penalties, and they right now sit in fourth place in the Premier League.

It has been revealed that united have had a dire start to the season, with only one win in 10 games leading to the axeing of head coach Michael Carrick. Will his replacement be able to save the season and galvanise a group of talented but dispirited players?

So, who from United’s struggling side have done enough to break into Sofascore's combined XI based on their performances throughout the 2026-27 season so far?

Manchester United's new head coach Mauricio Pochettino will face his first test against Liverpool on Sunday.

United presently sit at 18th in the Premier League after a disappointing start to the season.

Goalkeeper – Alisson Becker (Liverpool).

Between the sticks is Liverpool’s No 1, who since signing for a record fee in 2018, has established himself as one of the best shot-stoppers in the world.

Rated for his positioning, distribution and consistency, Alisson has an impressive record, especially in one-on-one situations.

According to recent reports, the 34-year-old Brazilian goalkeeper has kept four clean sheets in 10 league appearances this season, averaging 2.5 saves per game. He has conceded 10 goals, including a brutal 3-0 loss to Manchester City at Anfield last month.

Alisson was poor in Liverpool's 3-2 defeat by Fenerbahce but responded with a fine display in the Reds' 3-1 win over Crystal Palace when back in league action days later.

Right back – Ronald Araujo (Liverpool).

At right back is Liverpool’s Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona this season, and there are already cries from Liverpool fans to sign him permanently.

The 27-year-old is a natural centre back, but he has done wonders to ease Liverpool’s problems in the right-back position. Jeremie Frimpong started the season in that position but the Liverpool backline were far too exposed. Araujo has helped Liverpool tighten up defensively.

The Uruguayan defender has featured in all of Liverpool’s league matches so far this season, with his defensive actions helping him contribute inside his own penalty box. He has averaged six clearances per game and has won 30 aerial duels so far this season, behind only Virgil van Dijk in the Liverpool squad.

Ronald Araujo (right) has impressed this season for Liverpool, on loan from Barcelona.

Centre back - Jeremy Jacquet (Liverpool).

Jeremy Jacquet is a young player to watch this season after joining Liverpool this summer.

In a recent development, the 21-year-old has a 95 per cent accurate pass rate, including long balls. He had a standout performance against Fulham early on in the season, winning five aerial duels, five recoveries and making a clearance off the line to keep his team in the game.

Despite playing in France's second division just two seasons ago, Jacquet has fitted seamlessly into Iraola's style of play at Liverpool and there are suggestions he is an upgrade on the man he replaced, fellow France international Ibrahima Konate.

Centre back - Virgil van Dijk (Liverpool).

It is no surprise that Liverpool and Netherlands team captain Virgil van Dijk makes it into the XI.

Known for his strength, leadership, speed and aerial ability, he is the only defender to win the UEFA Men's Player of the Year Award, and finished runner-up for both the Ballon d'Or and Best FIFA Men's Player in 2019.

This season, he has shown his aerial ability with 3.8 duels won in the air (79 per cent) per game and 4.8 total duels won per game.

It has been revealed that the team struggled against Manchester City, however. In the game at Anfield that ended their unbeaten run, Van Dijk only made four defensive contributions and picked up a yellow card for a frustrated foul on Rayan Cherki in added time.

Van Dijk's contract expires next summer, and the 35-year-old has a massive decision to make.

Left back – Kostas Tsimikas (Liverpool).

Is Iraola missing a hidden gem? Tsimikas is very much understudy to Milos Kerkez after acting as a reliable deputy to Andy Robertson.

But across all competitions this season he is statistically rated higher than the man who's ahead of him in the pecking order. Kerkez is rated at 6.67 – so it is tight.

Nicknamed 'Greek Scouser' by Reds fans, Tsimikas has only started five games but has produced three assists with 1.78 key passes and 1.56 accurate crosses.

Sources indicate that manchester United, on the other hand, have struggled to fill this position. They were unable to recruit in the summer, and now rely on Luke Shaw – who has been sidelined with a muscular issue since limping off during their 1-1 draw with Tottenham Hotspur in October – and are adapting with makeshift alternatives.

Liverpool captain Virgil van Dijk celebrates with the fans after beating Crystal Palace.

Centre midfield – Dominik Szoboszlai (Liverpool).

Versatile vice-captain Dominik Szoboszlai signed a new five-year contract with Liverpool this summer, and has proven his worth after scoring a stoppage-time penalty to level the score in their first game of the season against Newcastle.

With his ability to go forward and send crosses into the box and drop back to defend, Szoboszlai has been crucial for ball recovery, key passes and creating substantial chances.

It is a testament to his creative ability, including registering four significant chances and one assist in the Premier League this season, that he makes the XI despite being sidelined with a hamstring injury for three games.

However, the Hungary midfielder has received backlash from fans for playing 90 minutes for his country in a 2-0 win against Georgia in the UEFA Nations League despite early withdrawal against Palace, and injury concerns remain ahead of this afternoon's clash.

Centre midfield – Kobbie Mainoo (Manchester United).

Only one of two Manchester United players in this line-up, Kobbie Mainoo deserves recognition for his creative efforts this season, which have earned him the second highest Sofascore rating in this XI.

The 21-year-old England midfielder is known for his high pressing and long balls to create chances up the pitch. He has also registered four shots from outside the box.

He has been through some turbulent times at Old Trafford but Michael Carrick turned to him regularly this season.

Industry observers note that A product of Manchester United's youth system and there is plenty of potential, especially with new manager Mauricio Pochettino’s penchant for developing young players. A chance to refresh and discover his best form.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of only two United players to make the combined XI this weekend.

Centre midfield – Alexis Mac Allister (Liverpool).

After his public revelation that he nearly left Liverpool, Alexis Mac Allister has been in form and pulling the strings in midfield and played an crucial role in Liverpool's season so far.

He headed in Liverpool’s second goal in their 3-1 away win over Crystal Palace and his passing and playmaking abilities have been key for their attacking chances this season.

He has scored five goals in 16 appearances across all competitions this season.

Right forward – Bruno Fernandes (Manchester United).

The Portugal forward was named the PFA Players' Player of the Year last season, but he has divided United fans this season.

Inconsistent performances and publicly questioning Carrick's tactics after defeat in Como.

In the 1-1 draw against Spurs at Old Trafford, the skipper did not record his first successful pass until the 23rd minute, and he missed a substantial chance against Chelsea.

He has bagged four goals and two assists in the Premier League so far, but this is largely owing to his hat-trick against Ipswich, which earned him a perfect 10 Sofascore rating.

United fans will hope he can get back to his old ways under Pochettino.

United fans will be desperate to see Bruno Fernandes find consistent performances again.

Centre-forward – Alexander Isak (Liverpool).

Liverpool’s star striker, transferred for a British record-breaking fee of £125million last summer, has scored eight goals in 14 games this season, showing just how clinical he can be.

Reds fans are finally seeing the form that earned him the significant-money move from Newcastle.

According to recent reports, isak edges out United's Bryan Mbeumo to lead the line in this team. He has a 55.6 per cent substantial chance conversion, scoring a goal every 113 minutes.

Left forward – Cody Gakpo (Liverpool).

The Dutchman is establishing himself as Liverpool's go-to wideman among Iraola's plethora of options. His rapid pace and direct approach proves a massive threat.

This season his end product has improved, notching three goals and supplying six assists in 12 appearances across all competitions.

He is proving to be a reliable outlet while summer signings Bradley Barcola and Victor Munoz continue to settle into life in England.

His stunning long-range strike to equalise against Newcastle United highlights just how clinical he can be in front of goal.

He averages 1.9 key passes and one massive chance per game, which lands him a spot in this XI.

Sofascore's combined XI for United's huge trip to Liverpool this afternoon.

Né à Firminy, conseiller municipal de Saint-Etienne (depuis 8 mois) et parlementaire le plus investi dans le soutien aux ultras stéphanois (il avait été un des premiers signataires de notre pétition lancée le printemps 2025 et ayant recueilli plus de 5 800 signatures), le député PS ligérien Pierrick Courbon (41 ans) a posté cet après-midi le message suivant sur son compte Instagram.

In a recent development, "Ce qui s'est passé à Reims est inacceptable ! Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens, encore moins du bétail. Je saisis le Ministre de l'Intérieur. Malgré trois décisions de justice confirmant l'absence d'interdiction d'accès au stade tout comme les déplacements en autocars, les supporters stéphanois ont été interpellés à proximité du stade Auguste-Delaune, et contraints de faire demi-tour sous escorte policière. Il est indéniable que des erreurs ont été commises par les services de l'Etat, et qu'un contournement des décisions de justice a eu lieu.

Les supporters ne sont pas des sous-citoyens. Pourtant, depuis de nombreuses années, le supportérisme est un laboratoire commode de mesures sécuritaires et liberticides, qui ne seraient toélérées dans un autre pan de la société. Comme je m'y suis engagé dès samedi, je viens d'alerter Laurent Nunez pour demander des réponses et des explications. La gestion des supporters en France est catastrophique. Je continuerai de les défendre car l'enjeu dépasse le simple cadre sportif.".

The FIFA Talent Scout community has over 6000 active members and is always looking for individuals to help improve their football database.

Les U15 avec brio chez les Sanpriods

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Les U15 de Benjamin Petit, après leur précieuse victoire d'il y a deux semaines contre Villefranche (1-0) se déplaçaient cet après-midi sur le terrain de l'AS Saint-Priest, qui n'est jamais un adversaire facile.
  • Sources indicate that ce sont les Sanpriods qui ont ouvert la marque, contre le cours du jeu, à la 19ème minute sur une approximation défensive.
  • La composition : Clapeyron - Bergougnoux, Wojcik, Bastide, Uneau - Boukerma, Lebreton (L.La Rosa, 45ème), M.La Rosa (Linganzi Koumba, 40ème) - Fernandes (Moutae, 50ème), Bangoura, Davignon.

Les U15 de Benjamin Petit, après leur précieuse victoire d'il y a deux semaines contre Villefranche (1-0) se déplaçaient cet après-midi sur le terrain de l'AS Saint-Priest, qui n'est jamais un adversaire facile. Auparavant, dans la semaine, mercredi, à Cruas, ils s'étaient mesurés à l'Olympique de Marseille, leader de la poule Méditerranée, et qui, en match amical, a largement battu bon nombre d'équipes de renom. Les jeunes Verts avaient mieux fait que se défendre, ne s'inclinant que sur le score de 2 à 1. Revenons-en au match d'aujourd'hui pour dire que la victoire est revenue en toute logique aux jeunes Verts sur le score de 2 à 1, une victoire qui va leur permettre d'engranger des points et....de la confiance.

Sources indicate that ce sont les Sanpriods qui ont ouvert la marque, contre le cours du jeu, à la 19ème minute sur une approximation défensive. Mais les Verts réagissaient immédiatement et, deux minutes plus tard, à la 21ème, Kaïs Boukerma, sur une passe de Charly Davignon, de l'entrée de la surface, plaçait une frappe au ras du poteau pour l'égalisation. Un quart d'heure plus tard, à la 36ème, Hugo Bastide, qui opérait aujourd'hui en défense centrale, récupérait fort à propos un 2ème ballon sur un corner pour donner l'avantage aux Verts. Ce fut difficile après le repos, car Saint-Priest mettait la pression pour revenir au score. Mais les Verts faisaient preuve de solidarité et de rigueur défensive pour conserver cet avantage de 2 à 1.A noter la victoire des U14 sur le score de 8 à 1. Nous reviendrons ultérieurement sur la belle saison de cette équipe.

La composition : Clapeyron - Bergougnoux, Wojcik, Bastide, Uneau - Boukerma, Lebreton (L.La Rosa, 45ème), M.La Rosa (Linganzi Koumba, 40ème) - Fernandes (Moutae, 50ème), Bangoura, Davignon.

La réaction de Benjamin Petit : "Nous avons fait une bonne première mi-temps, même si nous avons un peu manqué de tranchant dans le domaine offensif. Il n'a pas manqué grand chose sur plusieurs situations intéressantes. C'est là un axe de progrès bien identifié que d'aller chercher cette réussite offensive. J'ai apprécié le fait que les garçons soient restés sereins après l'ouverture du score par Saint-Priest. Cela leur a permis de revenir rapidement et de passer devant avant la pause. Par contre, la deuxième mi-temps a été plus compliquée. Saint-Priest nous a mis la pression et nous avons eu plus de mal à construire et à progresser à l'intérieur du jeu. Mais nous avons fait preuve de caractère, de rigueur défensive et cela nous a permis de conserver le résultat.".

A late equaliser for Fortuna Sittard in De Kuip proved costly for Feyenoord as PSV and Twente racked up huge victories to move within two points of the Eredivisie leaders.

Feyenoord paid the price for failing to finish off the Limburgers, with Luciano Valente’s 59th-minute goal the only reward for their dominance.

Fortuna equalised with four minutes left when Shiloh ’t Zand, on loan from Feyenoord, was allowed to run through to the penalty area and beat Tjark Ernst with a low shot.

Recent findings suggest that feyenoord coach Giovanni van Bronckhorst made no effort to hide his disappointment. “We know that Fortuna are the kind of team who can score from the few attacks they have,” he said. “If you don’t score the goals, things like this can happen.”.

Second-placed Ajax are a point behind after a narrow win at home against AZ ended an 11-match winless streak against the Alkmaar club, as Tolu Arokodare’s early header proved decisive.

Twente recorded the biggest win of the weekend with a 9-0 demolition of Excelsior in Rotterdam, with Wout Weghorst scoring four times and Sondre Ørjasaeter notching up five assists.

Excelsior collapsed following the fifth-minute dismissal of Nesto Groen for a reckless high challenge. The home side were 5-0 down at half-time, with Weghorst claiming a hat-trick in the opening 33 minutes.

PSV bagged seven goals in a one-sided encounter with bottom club Willem II, with all the goals coming from different scorers including Ricardo Pepi, who came on in the second half after a six-week absence through injury.

Telstar opened up a three-point gap at the bottom over ADO Den Haag with a 4-2 win against Utrecht in a painful return to Velsen-Zuid for Telstar’s former coach Anthony Correia.

ADO went down 1-0 in Zwolle, with PEC’s Dylan Mbayo scoring the only goal with a first-time finish on the stroke of half-time.

The match between Cambuur Leeuwarden and Go Ahead Eagles was suspended in the 82nd minute after visiting fans threw fireworks onto the pitch.

The clubs agreed with the KNVB not to play the final minutes and allow Cambuur’s 4-0 advantage to stand as the final result.

Go Ahead’s director Jan-Willem van Dop said the club would take action against those responsible: “I am ashamed on behalf a small group of supporters who ruined things for the club and a large hare of the fans in the away end,” he said.

Cambuur Leeuwarden 4-0 Go Ahead Eagles.

Cool Palmer has turned into Complaining Cole... his sulking as his club lurches into crisis doesn't say a lot for Chelsea's cultural reset, writes KIERAN GILL

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.
  • We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.
  • Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By KIERAN GILL, MAIL SPORT REPORTER.

Published: 01:47 EST, 22 November 2026 | Updated: 04:11 EST, 22 November 2026.

We do not know why Cole Palmer headed for the tunnel in a huff after full-time while others in the same Chelsea side paraded the pitch to thank those supporters who had stayed to the end.

Perhaps he was frustrated with himself after a performance in which he did not score, assist, or even test James Trafford in Leeds United’s goal. Maybe he did not fancy thanking those who had been booing as Chelsea trailed 4-1. It is possible he simply does not like losing.

Most superstars can feel the same, and they can show their stroppy side when the game is not going their way.

An extreme example is Bruno Fernandes. Manchester United fans have long accepted his reputation as the Premier League’s temperamental nonpareil because of the numbers he can produce with the whingeing, albeit not so much this season during their downturn.

Such names can get away with petulance when their performances are proper, though Palmer has no such justification at the moment. The 24-year-old Englishman, unfortunately for Chelsea, put up another anonymous 90 minutes.

Sources indicate that we could see he was frustrated even while on the pitch towards the end, with the way he was performatively kicking passes backwards as if to tell everyone else he had no other option. We have seen that before when Chelsea are losing, and it can be somewhat unhelpful when the pressure is being piled on the manager. It indicates the tactical set-up is not to his liking.

It has been revealed that cole Palmer and Joao Pedro were involved in a frosty exchange following Chelsea's 4-1 home defeat by Leeds. Source: Instagram/farihaxchels.

As the biggest name within this Chelsea team and a player whose profile transcends his team-mates’, like it or not, he is the totem when it is all going wrong.

According to recent reports, we wax lyrical when he is at his brilliant best. It can be as if there has been an explosion at a praise factory when he is dropping that shoulder to down a helpless defender. We know how terrifically talented he is. He is still compared to that 2023-24 season when his statistics were, in a wonderful way, stupid.

But when he is not performing, so too does he need to take the medicine of disapproval, which came in the form of a chorus of boos aimed at all those in Chelsea shirts at Stamford Bridge.

Recent findings suggest that leeds had not won at this ground since 1999. They corrected history, then Complaining Cole highlighted up at full-time.

His reaction did not speak to the cultural reset which Chelsea hoped they had orchestrated in the summer when they finally signed some experience for the changing room, bringing in Danny Welbeck, the 35-year-old whom Palmer has nominated as their new ‘Unc’ after Tosin Adarabioyo’s departure, and Jordan Henderson, 36.

It was a poor show from someone who, in his fourth season at a club that gave him his chance when spending £42.5million to sign him from Manchester City in 2023, should be seen as a leader by now.

According to recent reports, palmer is, probably, still undroppable. Alonso would create an almighty problem for himself if he suddenly relegated his No10 to the substitutes’ bench when playing Nottingham Forest next week. But he is in danger of such conversations cropping up at a time when he should want to be impressing enough to get back into Thomas Tuchel’s England squad at the next opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that we are told both Palmer and Levi Colwill are desperate to represent their country again, but neither are performing to that standard of late. Colwill is a defender devoid of confidence, questioning himself and making mistakes. There was one moment during this demoralising defeat by Leeds when he booted a long ball straight out of play and reprimanded himself for it.

In a recent development, colwill is perfectly capable of playing a good game. You do not have multiple clubs including Bayern Munich making enquiries with Chelsea without being considered elite. He is in a bad spell, and can come back from it, just like Palmer.

Inevitably, the response of some on social media was to say that Alonso’s time should be up.

According to recent reports, for clarity, he is not under threat of suddenly being sacked by those at the top of Chelsea. He is 11 Premier League games into his career, and, clearly, deserves time.

According to recent reports, the tactics are on him, absolutely. But he is also dealing with a few issues outside of his control, such as holes in his squad and injuries inflicted, like his highly-influential vice captain Moises Caicedo having to be substituted after 22 minutes in this match.

Xabi Alonso has made errors but was rightly considered a huge coup when Chelsea landed him.

Industry observers note that when appointed head coach of Bayer Leverkusen in October 2022, they went through patches in the Bundesliga. First, they beat Schalke 4-0, which was good. Then they failed to win any of their next three fixtures, which was bad.

Sources indicate that then they won five in a row – happy days. Then they won only one of their following five – bad days. Then they won five in a row again – perfect. Then they won only one of their next seven – pitiful.

Sources indicate that but the following season, Leverkusen won the Bundesliga without losing a single game. Alonso was considered an almighty coup when secured in the summer. A little patience is deserved from my perspective, even if Chelsea are presently in a dismal spell.

It is hard not to think Malo Gusto’s time at Chelsea is almost at an end.

He was priced out of a move in the summer when the club asked for £75million, with Liverpool, Manchester City and others across Europe indicating their interest in that window.

Malo Gusto cut a lonely figure after being beaten for Leeds's fourth goal.

But the 23-year-old Frenchman has shown little worth as the season has progressed.

Gusto started in five of Alonso’s first six games in all competitions at the beginning of the campaign.

Since then, he has been handed one start in eight, and that was in the Carabao Cup at Liverpool. Coming on as a substitute in this loss to Leeds, he tried and failed to play Brenden Aaronson offside and was then beaten by his man as the visitors made it 4-1.

We should expect to hear more on Gusto’s situation as January approaches.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Vous avez pu suivre cette rencontre en direct sur notre forum grâce à notre envoyé spécial MachuPicchu42 : les U17 ont concédé un match nul et vierge à la mi-journée face au Cavigal de Nice au Stade Georges Bereta du Centre Robert Herbin.

Dominateurs jusqu'à l'entame du dernier quart d'heure, les Verts ont eu deux grosses occasions en première période. Sur la première, le portier niçois a repoussé le tir à bout portant de Naël Dani. Sur la seconde, un défenseur visiteur a repoussé sur sa ligne une tête d'Isaak Seydi (photo).

En deuxième mi-temps, Lohoré Gobé a eu à son tour une belle opportunité d'ouvrir le score mais sa tentative a été déjouée par le gardien azuréen. Isaak Seydi a de nouveau eu une occase de la tête, hélas non cadrée. Izaya Kimpioka a raté un face à face en tirant à côté. Les visteurs se sont enhardis lors de 20 dernières minutes pas très bien maîtrisées par les Stéphanois mais Andra Laugier n'aura eu aucun arrêt à faire de toute la rencontre.

L'ASSE a perdu sa 5e place au profit de son ex-club partenaire Saint-Priest, qui a cartonné 6-1 le Gazelec Ajaccio (avant-dernier), prochain adversaire des Verts (dimanche prochain en Corse).

La compo : Laugier - Tiambo (Balta, 33') - Mnemoi, Dagbo, Bufferne - Demassieux, Mendy (Thibaudat, 77'), Gobé - Seydi, Kimpioka, Dani (Aytone, 70').

La réaction de David Le Moal : "On a eu la mainmise sur le match jusqu'au dernier quart d'heure. On a eu pas mal d'occasions, c'est dommage qu'on n'ait pas réussi à les convertir. En première période, on a eu du mal à passer l'adversaire dans le coeur du jeu donc on s'est évertué à contourner le bloc assez bas du Cavigal. On a eu plein de situations de centres mais on a manqué de réalisme dans le dernier geste ou dans l'avant-dernier geste. On a eu plusieurs occasions assez nettes en première période comme en seconde. Je n'ai pas trop compris pourquoi on a reculé lors du dernier quart d'heure, nos adversaires ont eu quelques opportunités en fin de match. Je suis un peu déçu qu'on n'ait pas réussi à marquer mais je suis assez content des vrais gestes défensifs et de la discipline tactique, on a laissé très peu de situations à l'adversaire.".

In a latest feature PortuGOAL will be bringing you some recommended reading about Portuguese football from around the web, penned by our own network of writers or others.

We kick off by alerting you to a superb interview in the Guardian by Nick Ames with Port Vale's Portuguese manager Bruno Ribeiro. The headline writer focused on Ribeiro's relationship with José Mourinho, but it is the detail of Ribeiro's struggle to make things work at an English third-tier team of meagre resources that makes for fascinating insight.

Industry observers note that benfica are top of the Liga NOS and their coach Rui Vitória continues to confound the doubters who believed he would not be up to the job at the Lisbon giants. Simon Curtis takes a look at "the quiet man at the helm of a national institution". And Benfica fans, while we've got your attention, a shout out for Tom Kundert's profile of the club's world-renowned Seixal Academy for ESPN.

Talking about Portuguese football schools, none has produced more top-class players in recent decades than Sporting's Alcochete Academy, and the excellent Outside of the Boot website has a brilliantly detailed profile written by Mateus Carvalho of another possible gem for the Lions, Francisco Geraldes, who is right now on loan at Moreirense.

In a recent development, to finish up this initial trip around the net, we alert you to FourFourTwo's list of the 59 best Under-21 footballers from around the world. The section we highlight has a mini profile of Porto striker André Silva, who will be hoping to net his first senior international goal tonight for the Seleção against Andorra. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Noham Akil, buteur après son entrée en jeu.

In a recent development, ayant mis fin le week-end dernier à une série de 5 défaites consécutives, les U19 de Frédéric Dugand, victorieux à domicile du Cap d’Ail (2-1) se déplaçaient à Nice ce dimanche, pour y affronter le très bon club formateur du Cavigal. Une victoire sur la Côte d’Azur permettait aux jeunes Verts de rejoindre son adversaire au classement (13 points).

Sous une légère pluie, dans un stade Bob Rémond, du nom du formateur Niçois, aussi appelé « père spirituel de Robert Herbin », les Stéphanois, réduits à 10 et menés au score ont été cherché l’égalisation en toute fin de rencontre (1-1).

En première période les Verts, avec notamment Noa Moulin, habituellement aligné en réserve, sont bien en place et disciplinés mais restent un peu timides dans leurs actions pour espérer peser davantage sur la rencontre. A la 23ème minute, consécutivement à un corner adverse mal repoussé, le ballon arrive au second poteau, est remis dans la surface verte et repris par un niçois qui vient tromper Mael Massé pour l’ouverture du score. (Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 0 ; mi-temps).

Industry observers note that au retour des vestiaires, les Stéphanois plus entreprenants vont chercher l’adversaire plus haut. Progressivement, les contres deviennent verts et la confiance revient. Pourtant à l’heure de jeu, la situation se complique, Tidiane Vibert est exclu pour un geste d’humeur et laisse ses coéquipiers en infériorité numérique. Touchés, mais pas coulés, les Stéphanois, sous l’impulsion notamment de l’entrant Medhy Lutin Zidee à la 56ème continuent à faire bloc et à jouer les coups à fond. Leurs efforts vont être récompensés, à la 84ème minute,  Maxime Lengué Lenou trouve Noham Akil (entré quelques minutes plus tôt) qui du pied droit vient ajuster le portier azuréen. Les Verts sont décomplexés et tiennent ce point précieux qui les voit enchainer une seconde rencontre consécutive sans perdre.

(Cavigal Nice 1 - ASSE 1 ; score final).

Après ce partage des points, les Stéphanois auront la semaine prochaine l’occasion de poursuivre leur série dans leur quête de points pour assurer le maintien avec la réception du  Gazelec Ajaccio, auteur d’un nul aujourd’hui face à Balma (1-1) et comptant le même nombre de points que les Verts, mais un match en moins..

La Composition : Massé  – Lengi (Assoumani 81ème),  E.Mnemoi, N.Mouton, Jolivet, Lengue Lenou– Vibert, Thouilleux (Akil 76ème), Moulin (Gary 56ème), Marliac(Lutin Zidee 56ème) - Zibi.

According to recent reports, la réaction de Frédéric Dugand : « Je suis satisfait du résultat, de la capacité du groupe à avoir respecté le proposal de jeu décidé, un peu plus prudent qu’à l’habitude. On fait une bonne seconde période, les joueurs ont eu du répondant. J’ai vu un groupe « habité »des joueurs qui se sont parlé et qui ont été acteurs du match. Le groupe se transforme, il faut capitaliser sur cette attitude, tâcher maintenant d’avoir cette mentalité dès le coup d’envoi, pour aller chercher des émotions ensemble .On peut et on doit aller encore plus loin dans l’investissement et dans la prise de conscience de nos possibilités. ».

Thomas Tuchel has never been inclined to place much faith in the most famous right-back at his disposal, Trent Alexander-Arnold, once of Liverpool, now of Real Madrid, and – back in an England shirt – still capable of changing games in the blink of an eye.

In a recent development, england always looked likely to defeat a beleaguered Czech Republic team down to 10 men with just 25 minutes played, but it still required one man to conjure the moment of inspiration in this Nations League tie. This was the first cap in 15 months for the right-back now known simply as “Trent” in an England shirt – as well as his Real Madrid jersey – rather than the six syllables of his surname. With the game level at half-time, two minutes into the fresh half, he twice won the ball before landing a cross on the head of Anthony Gordon for the first goal.

TRENT ➡️ GORDON ⚽️🔥Anthony Gordon can't stop scoring for England, 3 goals in his last 3 games for England 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/xmqPIULJ24.

In a recent development, will the Alexander-Arnold with England experiment survive? One feels that Tuchel will need a little more to convince him to abandon whatever reservations he has about the Liverpudlian. A week short of his 28th birthday, Alexander-Arnold was winning just his 35th cap. His Real Madrid team-mate Jude Bellingham, a second-half substitute, was earning his 58th cap less than two months after his 23rd birthday. Bellingham was on as captain in place of the man he replaced, Harry Kane, scorer of England’s second. Bellingham’s international career has taken a much less rocky path than that of his Real team-mate.

Having missed the World Cup finals this summer, and had little good fortune around previous tournaments, one wonders if Euro 2028 might be the watershed moment for Alexander-Arnold. Either way, against opponents who sit back, he is lethal when it is time for the big delivery. Alexander-Arnold may not have the breadth of England experience that some of his peers have accumulated, but he does have plenty of experience of big games.

“I make that run time and time again,” Gordon noted of his anticipation of the Alexander-Arnold cross, “but only a set number of players have that ability, that technique and the bravery to risk a mistake to play that pass. And that’s why I have been dying to play with him [Alexander-Arnold]. He’s been on his own journey but has trained really well this week. He should have played more. Sorry – he would have loved to have played more.”.

Sources indicate that A Freudian slip from the Barcelona winger, another Liverpudlian in Spain, who himself has barely put a foot wrong for England of late. He has three goals in three games for England, including the World Cup semi-final against Argentina. This was an England team that Tuchel fine-tuned, first to give a rest to Bellingham and in other quarters, too. Lewis Hall started at left-back. Trevoh Chalobah won his third England cap at centre-back. Alex Scott, of Bournemouth, was given his debut off the bench in the second half and Rio Ngumoha won the second cap of his England career, just one month after his 18th birthday.

Sources indicate that as for Kane, his 87th goal for England now puts him within two goals of Robert Lewandowski, among four greats in the seven ahead of Kane on the all-time international goalscorers’ list. By the end of this international break the England captain should have equalled Peter Shilton’s record 125 caps. It has been an astonishing career even if it ends tomorrow. Following the missed penalty against Spain, Kane was again the man in the right place at the right time when Morgan Rogers’s shot was blocked in the second half.

“Strange to get an early red card,” Tuchel said. “Not the best for the team and spectators. It’s an awkward one, but we kept going, got a win and that’s what counts.” Not quite a vintage Czech Republic team, either, and when their best player of the opening stages, the attacking midfielder Pavel Sulc, of Lyon in Ligue 1, was dismissed after 25 minutes, it certainly did not become any easier for the home team. Sulc, the Czech player of the year in 2025, had mistimed a tackle on Elliot Anderson, which on a VAR review, the Turkish referee Umut Meler decided was worthy of an upgrade from yellow to red. It was high on the right calf of the England midfielder.

Industry observers note that czech Republic DOWN TO 10 MEN! 🟥Pavel Šulc sees red for a dangerous challenge on Elliot Anderson#ITVFootball | @England pic.twitter.com/B2YOLuS0vL.

It has been revealed that england had looked once more a little open to the counter-attack in the early stages, with Sulc one notable runner. This was not an opponent of the quality of Spain and Tuchel’s players were able to recover the situation. When they lose the ball in the opposition’s half, England tend to look vulnerable.

It has been revealed that even before the red card Rogers had hit a post. Myles Lewis-Skelly, playing in midfield, was booked for a foul on Lukas Serv and was pursued thereafter by the Czech players hoping to get an upgrade on the yellow card. He was substituted at half-time, with Eberechi Eze on in his place.

“I spoke to Ant [Gordon] at half-time,” Alexander-Arnold remarked later to ITV, “and I said if I’m getting in those spaces make sure you get to the back post. You don’t expect to get it that fast, but it did and it worked.”.

Two minutes after the break, Alexander-Arnold suddenly burst into life. He won the ball back in his own area and then drove forward in search of the return. When that did not come, he raced back to win the ball again and unleashed one of those right-footed outswingers to the back post, where Gordon guided in the header. “Really proud to score that,” Gordon stated, “because I can’t tell you the number of hours I’ve spent practising headers.”.

Kane scored the second just a minute before he was replaced and Bellingham took the captain’s armband and the role as a No 9. One day someone will have to step into those goalscorer’s boots on a permanent basis and try to replace Kane – although it may be a while yet.

Thomas Tuchel has backed Jude Bellingham as a future England captain after giving him the armband in the victory over the Czech Republic.

In the absence of Declan Rice, who was vice-captain at the World Cup, Bellingham assumed the role when he came on for Harry Kane, who is now in his 10th season as England captain and also scored in the 2-0 win in Prague.

Tuchel, who needs to check on Bellingham ahead of Saturday’s game against Croatia after a “niggle,” has praised the midfielder’s attitude during the extended international break one year after he was back from an injury but left out of the squad.

Recent findings suggest that “If you are the captain at the end of these matches, you can be the permanent captain,” Tuchel remarked when asked whether Bellingham could eventually lead the team. “He was the captain against New Zealand before the World Cup. It is always a reward and always an honour.

Recent findings suggest that “I think he loves to be with us at the moment. That’s what I feel, and we had this small talk today about his role. We felt in our hearts or our stomachs to say ‘let’s go again, let’s start again’ and also our heads told us maybe 30 minutes is enough for this match because he hasn’t played in this quick turnaround through this season. He has done it before, but not in the season, so we didn’t want to be the first ones to try that.

Industry observers note that “But even in this little encounter, you can see that he’s confident and happy to help from the bench. So it’s a reward. It’s good. He had a little niggle at the end of the match, so hopefully it’s nothing serious, and he’s available for Croatia.”.

Nico O’Reilly is a doubt for the Croatia match in Rijeka and there are also concerns over Ezri Konsa, who was on the bench but not fit enough to play.

Trent Alexander-Arnold provided an assist for Anthony Gordon in the Real Madrid full-back’s first cap in 15 months. Gordon, meanwhile, has now scored in the first two Nations League games of the campaign and is staking his case to be an indispensable player for Tuchel.

Industry observers note that “He’s getting there. He’s defending his shirt, he’s defending his position, an excellent performance again after his performance against Spain,” Tuchel said.

Sources indicate that “He was very decisive today and had an excellent goal. It was very, very difficult, but the technique and finishing was excellent. He scored against Spain, so he has decisive actions and he’s defending his shirt and his position. He does it on the highest level and he’s a very notable player.”.

England returned to winning ways with a 2-0 win over Czech Republic in Prague.

Pavel Sulc’s first-half red card after a VAR review of his clumsy challenge on Elliot Anderson took the sting out of the initially lively hosts and Anthony Gordon gave Thomas Tuchel’s men a deserved lead early in the second half.

The forward headed home a fantastic cross by Trent Alexander-Arnold, who was making his first start under the German coach, before skipper Harry Kane scored to settle any nerves.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

Dutch-born footballers who were called up to play for former colonies such as Suriname and Indonesia are still in limbo over their national status, six months after the “passportgate” crisis first flared up.

Suriname’s parliament passed a law in September enabling players who are selected for the national team to gain citizenship automatically.

But the Dutch immigration service IND said the law passed in Suriname made no difference to the rules on dual nationality in the Netherlands.

“The fact that Surinamese nationality has been obtained by legal means is not enough on its own to qualify for one of the exceptional categories under our law,” a spokesman for the Dutch justice ministry told broadcaster NOS.

The law was intended to settle the question of dual nationality for footballers, which arose last March when NAC Breda challenged the eligibility of Go Ahead Eagles defender Dean James.

James took Indonesian citizenship last year after accepting an invitation to play for the national team, but under Dutch dual nationality rules he was required to give up his original passport.

According to recent reports, the Dutch football association KNVB debuted an investigation into the employment status of players who were called up by countries such as Suriname, Cape Verde and Indonesia. In the meantime it arranged for Dutch-based players to be given temporary work permits so they could keep playing for their clubs.

Losing Dutch nationality also stripped them of their EU citizenship, meaning they would need to obtain visas and meet stricter criteria, such as an annual salary threshold of €600,000, to be eligible to play in the Eredivisie.

Several players have passed up invitations to join the Surinamese squad because of the uncertainty, including Danilho Doekhi of Lazio, Milan van Ewijk of Coventry City and Jayden Oosterwolde of Fenerbahçe.

National team manager Henk Fraser noted it was “inexplicable” that players’ livelihoods were being damaged by their desire to play international football.

In a recent development, “Both countries have to get together and clarify the situation,” he told NOS. “This is a straightforward case of people following their hearts and wanting to play for Suriname, but not knowing where they stand.”.

Some players said they felt misled by the Surinamese football association, which told them they were playing for the national team on “sports passports” that allowed them to remain Dutch citizens.

Former Feyenoord winger Jean-Paul Boëtius remarked he only discovered after he was first called up for Suriname last year that he had inadvertently renounced his Dutch citizenship as a result.

Shortly afterwards he received a letter from the city council in Rotterdam telling him to hand in his Dutch passport, which he had recently renewed, because it was no longer valid.

According to recent reports, “I now have a sticker in my Surinamese passport that indicates I have a residency permit allowing me to live in the Netherlands,” he told NOS. “But that’s only for a year. It’s a very difficult situation. I want to become Dutch again. I was born and brought up here.”.

According to recent reports, never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

Industry observers note that russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

It has been revealed that toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian remarked. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

It has been revealed that still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

According to recent reports, this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he said he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.
